# Usage report: per-model provider status table with next-check time

## Goal (user story)

As a proxy operator reading the daily usage report, I want a table immediately
after the performance-metrics scorecard showing the **current routing status of
every provider entry in every model chain, and when that status will next be
checked or re-evaluated**, so that a silently deadlocked provider is visible in
the report the morning it happens instead of being found by hand weeks later.

## Problem

The report can say *how often* the chain fell back and to where, but it cannot
answer the question the operator actually asks when fallback is high: **"which
provider is unavailable right now, why, and when does that change?"** The
statuses that suppress a provider are already computed by the resolver but
never surfaced:

| Gate (evaluated in this order, `proxy/proxy/provider.py`) | Line | Suppresses the entry for |
|---|---|---|
| `usage_limit_account` (same account already exhausted this request) | ~11533 | the rest of that request |
| `quota_exhausted` / `dispatch_on_balance` (proactive quota snapshot) | ~11546 | until the blocking quota window resets |
| `usage_limit_reset_pending` (persisted account quarantine) | ~11560 | until `reset_at` (minutes → **weeks**) |
| `quota_hard_stop` | ~11606 | until the monthly window resets |
| `provider_cooldown` | ~11628 | 30 s – 300 s |
| `outside its available_times` | ~11647 | until the next window edge |

The gap is not theoretical. On 2026-11-12 05:46:05 `opencode-go` returned HTTP
402 `Insufficient balance`; the proxy recorded a `balance_exhaustion`
quarantine bounded by the **monthly plan** reset — **2026-11-23 08:45:55** —
and then skipped the entry on every request for eleven days. Nothing in the
report showed it: every nightly run looked normal, the account simply never
appeared, and the deadlock was only found by reading `proxy-state.json` by
hand and grepping `usage_limit_reset_pending` out of the live log. A single
table with `opencode-go | usage_limit_reset_pending | next checked
2026-11-23 08:45` would have made it obvious on the first morning.

Visibility is also the cheaper alternative to automating early quarantine
release: the operator can see that a top-up will not be picked up until the
plan window rolls over, and act (or not) deliberately.

## Scope

In scope (usage-report skill only — `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/`):

- a new `## Provider status` table rendered **immediately after** the
  `## Performance metrics summary` scorecard table (`scripts/reporting.py`,
  currently line ~1384) and **before** `## Performance metric details`
  (line ~1481);
- a new deterministic module (suggested `scripts/provider_status.py`) that
  derives the rows; it must not re-implement the resolver's gate semantics —
  see *Design notes*;
- an additive `--json` block (`provider_status`);
- tests (unit + fixture-rendered) and the skill's `SKILL.md` / `REFERENCE.md`
  updates.

Out of scope:

- changing any proxy routing behaviour, quarantine duration or probe cadence
  (this item is observational only — it must not alter what the proxy does);
- adding a network call to the proxy, Prometheus or any other live service;
- alerting/paging on status (the report row is the deliverable).

## Table shape

One table, ordered by model chain (config order) then by chain position, so
each model's fallback sequence reads top-down:

| Model | # | Provider entry | Status | Detail | Next check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| plan | 1 | local-qwen3 | eligible | — | next request |
| plan | 2 | opencode-go-3 | quota_exhausted | monthly 100.0 %, resets in 10.3 h | 2026-11-17 10:07 |
| plan | 3 | opencode-go-2 | quota_exhausted | monthly 100.0 %, resets in 13 days | 2026-11-30 00:05 |
| plan | 4 | opencode-go | usage_limit_reset_pending | balance exhaustion, window unknown | 2026-11-23 08:45 |
| plan | 5 | munitoai-free | usage_limit_reset_pending | window unknown | 2026-11-17 00:02 |
| plan | 6 | munitoai | outside available_times | next window 10:00–23:00 UTC | 2026-11-17 10:00 |
| plan | 7 | deepseek-flash | outside available_times | next window 10:00–00:00 UTC | 2026-11-17 10:00 |

`Status` is the **first suppressing gate** the resolver would hit (the order
above), or `eligible` when none does. `Detail` carries the gate's own evidence
(quota window + percent, quarantine window + reason, cooldown key and
remaining seconds, or the window being waited for). `Next check` is the
instant the suppression is expected to lift, or the next point at which the
proxy will re-evaluate it — defined in the next section so the column is never
ambiguous.

An `Events in window` column (skip count per entry, derived from the existing
`Skipping provider=` parse) is optional; add it only if it costs no extra log
pass.

## Semantics of `Next check`

The column must state *how* it was derived, because three different mechanisms
answer "when next":

| Status | `Next check` | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| `eligible` | `next request` | the resolver's gate checks run per request; nothing is pending |
| `provider_cooldown` | cooldown expiry instant | `provider_unavailable_until` in the provider state file |
| `usage_limit_reset_pending` (hard / window-derived) | quarantine `reset_at` | `usage_reset_at` in the state file; revalidated from the next quota poll, so the instant is the *earliest* lift, not a guarantee |
| `usage_limit_reset_pending` (soft / guessed) | `now + min(probe interval, reset_at)` | the self-healing probe cadence (`_USAGE_LIMIT_PROBE_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, 300 s) is what actually re-checks these |
| `quota_exhausted` / `quota_hard_stop` | the blocking window's `resetsAt` | the last `quota poll ok` line for that account (`seconds_to_reset`) |
| `outside available_times` | the next window edge in UTC | `available_times` from `proxy/config.yaml`, including overnight wraparound (e.g. `22:00-02:00`) |
| any status with no usable evidence | `unknown` | never a fabricated instant |

## Design notes and assumptions

**Data sources (all local files / already-parsed log lines — no network call):**

1. `proxy/config.yaml` — the model chains, entry order, `available_times`,
   `use_balance`, `api_key_env`, `quota_poll_interval_seconds`.
2. `proxy/provider-state.json` — `provider_unavailable_until` (cooldowns) and
   `usage_reset_at` (account quarantines). Path is overridable by
   `LLAMA_PROXY_PROVIDER_STATE_FILE` (`proxy/proxy/provider.py:296`); the
   analyser must honour that environment variable and treat a missing file as
   "no pending suppression", not an error.
3. The **last** `quota poll ok account=...` line in the analysis window per
   account — the only persisted view of the in-process quota snapshot. Poll
   cadence is `quota_poll_interval_seconds` (900 s), so a window shorter than
   that may legitimately have none.

**Single source of truth (hard requirement).** The gate order and the
reason strings must not be duplicated as prose in the report module. Either
import the constants from `proxy/provider.py` (the skill already imports
`MEASURED_CACHE_DEFICIT_REASON` this way — see the capacity-signals section of
`SKILL.md`, including the PEP 420 namespace-package caveat it documents), or
add a small canonical `GATE_ORDER` tuple there that both the resolver and the
analyser consume. A test must fail if the two orders diverge.

**Assumption A1 — row granularity.** "Each model" is read as *each model chain
(`plan`, `author`, `code`, …) × each provider entry in it*, because the entry
is the unit the gates act on and the chain position is what makes a dead entry
fatal. `opencode-go` therefore appears once per chain it belongs to. If the
operator prefers one row per distinct entry with a `Model chains` column
instead, that is a rendering change only — the derivation is identical.

**Assumption A2 — reference instant.** All relative figures are computed
against the report window's end (the analysis `--end`, default now), stated in
the section's intro sentence, so a re-run over an old window reproduces the
same table rather than silently using wall-clock time.

**Assumption A3 — live-state caveat.** `provider-state.json` and the last
quota poll are point-in-time snapshots, not window aggregates. The section
intro must say so in one sentence: the table describes the state at report
generation, not the state during the window. This is the same honesty
discipline the report already applies to the GPU row and the engine
cross-check.

**Assumption A4 — local entries.** `local-qwen3` has no endpoint and no quota
account. It is rendered with `eligible` and `next request`, or with the
existing local-route cooldown reason when one is recorded — it must not be
dropped from the table, because a reader comparing chains needs the whole
sequence.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — `report.md` contains `## Provider status` immediately after the
  `## Performance metrics summary` table and before `## Performance metric
  details`. A test asserts the section order, not just presence.
- **AC2** — The table has one row per (model chain, provider entry) in
  `proxy/config.yaml` order and chain order, and a test asserts the row count
  and order equal the config's for a fixture config.
- **AC3** — `Status` is the *first* suppressing gate in the resolver's order;
  a unit test covers an entry suppressed by two mechanisms simultaneously
  (e.g. `usage_limit_reset_pending` and `provider_cooldown`) and asserts the
  earlier gate wins.
- **AC4** — `Next check` is derived per the semantics table, with unit tests
  for: cooldown expiry, hard quarantine `reset_at`, soft/guessed quarantine
  capped at the probe interval, quota window reset from the last
  `quota poll ok` line, an `available_times` window later the same UTC day,
  and an overnight window that wraps past midnight.
- **AC5** — The reproduction from this item's *Problem* section renders as
  `opencode-go | usage_limit_reset_pending | 2026-11-23 08:45` from a fixture
  built on the 2026-11-12 state file — i.e. the incident is visible.
- **AC6** — Degradation is named, never fabricated: with a missing state file,
  no `quota poll ok` line, an unparseable `available_times` entry, or an
  unknown status string, the cell reads `unknown` and the run still exits 0.
  A test covers each of the four.
- **AC7** — `--json` carries an additive `provider_status` block with the same
  rows (`model`, `position`, `entry`, `status`, `detail`, `next_check`,
  `next_check_basis`) and no existing key changes. A test asserts the Markdown
  table and the JSON rows agree.
- **AC8** — Gate order and reason strings have a single source of truth: a
  test fails if `provider_status`'s gate order or a reason string diverges from
  the proxy resolver's.
- **AC9** — No network call is added: a test asserts the module performs no
  HTTP request (the skill's `tests/conftest.py` network seam already blocks one,
  so the test proves it is never attempted) and the 05:00 cron line is
  unchanged.
- **AC10** — An empty window (no logs) still renders a valid table from config
  + state alone, with `unknown` where log evidence is needed, and the 05:00
  cron exits 0.
- **AC11** — `SKILL.md` gains a `## Provider status` section (what the columns
  mean, the `Next check` semantics table, the live-state caveat) and
  `REFERENCE.md` documents the data sources and the `--json` schema; both are
  reviewed against the rendered output in the same change.
- **AC12** — No proxy behaviour change: the diff touches only
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/` (plus, at most, one extracted constant in
  `proxy/proxy/provider.py` for AC8) and the full test suite passes.

## Traceability

- Discovered while root-causing the 2026-11-16 `opencode-go` deadlock (HTTP 402
  `Insufficient balance` → `balance_exhaustion` quarantine until the monthly
  plan reset 2026-11-23, skipped on every request for eleven days).
  `discovered-from` that investigation; no upstream work item exists for it.
- Related: LP-0MW0FU5Z6006A4P3 (performance metrics scorecard — the table this
  section follows), LP-0MVN4LCQJ0034S5S and LP-0MW2SQNHJ0044PV6 (usage-report
  feature precedent: summary table + detail section + honest degradation),
  LP-0MVU8O4EL005IYP9 (Local capacity signals — the shared-derivation and
  named-unavailability pattern to follow), LP-0MW46PAU4006SK7Z /
  LP-0MW46PBWL008T317 (`use_balance` and balance exhaustion — the semantics the
  `Status`/`Detail` columns must report), LP-0MUQTCMW2001VXH8 (self-healing
  probe cadence that defines the soft-quarantine `Next check`).
- Deliberately **not** done here: automating early release of a balance
  quarantine. This item only makes the state visible.

## Impact

The operator can see, in the daily report, which provider is unavailable, why,
and the exact moment it will be re-checked — so an eleven-day silent deadlock
is a single glance instead of weeks of unnoticed fallback.

## Problem statement

The first proxy-initiated `/slots` poll after a proxy restart can fire
*before* child-port discovery has succeeded, so it takes the router-port
fallback path: it logs a `slots_child_port_unavailable` WARNING
(`model=Qwen3`, `source=log_signal`), increments
`llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
and traverses the router (`:8080`) instead of the model child port.

Consequence: every 24 h post-restart verification window on this surface
starts with a guaranteed chat-model fallback, which fails a zero-tolerance
"chat-model fallback delta == 0" acceptance criterion even when
steady-state operation is clean.

## Evidence (measured, LP-0MVP7HX2S008IU57 window 2026-11-16T15:20:47Z → 2026-11-17T15:20:47Z)

The window is anchored to the proxy restart (`pid 3720326`, `lstart`
2026-11-16T15:20:47Z), so the process-lifetime counter delta *is* the window
delta. In `proxy.log.2026-11-16_15`, immediately after the boot sequence
(`Started TTS server`, `death capture: armed`, `Slot occupancy sampler
started (interval 10.0s)`):

```text
2026-11-16 15:20:51,411 - WARNING - slots_child_port_unavailable: no model child port discovered for model=Qwen3 (source=log_signal); falling back to router port 8080 — every proxy-initiated /slots poll will traverse t...
2026-11-16 15:20:51,435 - WARNING - llama-server --version returned 127
2026-11-16 15:20:51,560 - INFO - Adopted running llama-server (model=router parallel=1 router_mode=True); preserving warm prompt cache
```

- Only **one** `Starting LLama Proxy Server` marker in the whole window
  (15:20:49.786, the anchor process's own boot) ⇒ no in-window restart.
- `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
  = **1.0** for a process that started at the window start.
- Exactly **one** `slots_child_port_unavailable` line in the window, at
  window start **+4.4 s**; **zero** for the remaining 23 h 59 m 56 s.
- The same transient is visible in the earlier LP-0MVVLKPBM007F6U6 window
  (3 × `model=Qwen3`, each one within 3 s of a restart) — i.e. it is
  restart-correlated, not busy-child-correlated.

## Desired change

Make the boot-time slot poll child-port-aware: either

1. retry/defer the first slot poll until child-port discovery has resolved
   (bounded backoff), or
2. mark the poll as a boot transient so the fallback counter / WARNING are
   not incremented before discovery has had a chance to succeed.

The zero-tolerance signal (`llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total` + the
`slots_child_port_unavailable` WARNING) must stay usable as a *regression*
signal — a boot-time increment makes a clean 24 h window indistinguishable
from one real discovery regression.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — After a proxy restart, the first proxy-initiated `/slots` poll
  does not increment `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
  and does not emit `slots_child_port_unavailable` when the model child port
  becomes discoverable within the boot window.
- **AC2** — A genuine discovery regression (child port never discoverable)
  still increments the counter and emits the WARNING; covered by a test.
- **AC3** — Reproduced by a test: boot sequence with a not-yet-ready child
  port ⇒ no fallback counter increment; child port never ready ⇒ counter
  increments once per throttled interval.
- **AC4** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the change.
- **AC5** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A restarted proxy no longer looks like it had a child-port discovery
regression on its very first slot poll, so a clean 24 h window can pass the
zero-tolerance fallback check.

## Goal

Land the synthetic-log fixtures and failing tests that define the eviction-attribution split and the `cache-ram` x `ctx-checkpoints` trade-off table, so the parent's AC1 and AC2 implementation is driven by tests rather than written first and characterised afterwards. No production change and no `models.ini` change in this slice.

## Context

`scripts/prompt_cache_analysis.py` already parses llama-server logs (prompts, prompt tokens requested/reused/prefilled, full prefills small/large, evictions and their sizes, cache-state samples, checkpoint sizes) and `tests/test_prompt_cache_analysis.py` drives it from inline synthetic corpora written to a temp dir. What is missing is any notion of a *match* between an evicted cache entry and a later full prefill, and any ability to vary the checkpoint term in the recommendation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A synthetic corpus exercises the eviction-attribution join: an eviction line for a known entry size, followed within the match window by a full prefill of a prompt whose token count matches the evicted entry, and the test asserts the prefill is classified as eviction-attributable.
- Tests cover the conservative cases and assert each classification: no preceding eviction -> genuinely new tokens; prefill outside the match window -> not attributed; prefill whose size differs beyond the stated tolerance -> not attributed; a `forcing full prompt re-processing` task -> classified by the same rule, not by the message.
- Tests assert the summary contract for attribution: eviction-attributable full-prefill count, eviction-attributable prompt-token volume, eviction-attributable share of prefilled tokens, genuinely-new prompt-token volume, and the unattributed remainder; the four buckets must sum to the prefilled total.
- Tests assert the trade-off table contract: one row per candidate (`cache-ram`, `ctx-checkpoints`) pair, each row carrying prompts held, per-prompt state, the checkpoint term, killed prompts, the checkpoint resume value and MiB per prompt; halving `ctx-checkpoints` halves the per-prompt checkpoint term in the assertion.
- Tests assert the committed artifact's `meta` block records the corpus file list and the named window, so a before/after comparison is reproducible.
- The red run is recorded in a work-item comment (`/skill:test` changed-scope run) before implementation begins.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add fixture builders next to the existing `SYNTH` corpus: one attributable eviction, one genuinely-new session, one out-of-window eviction, one size-mismatch case, one forced-full-reprefill case.
2. Drive the new assertions through the script's CLI and `--json` output (same pattern as the existing tests) rather than importing internals where practical.
3. Assert the trade-off table as rendered markdown plus its JSON form, so the table is consumable by a doc and by the pinning test.
4. Record the red run in a comment with the exact `/skill:test` invocation and date.

## Definition of Done

Red tests committed (each failing for the intended reason, not import errors); `/skill:test` changed-scope run recorded; build -> changed-scope tests -> commit order respected.

**Key Files:**
- `tests/test_prompt_cache_analysis.py`
- `scripts/prompt_cache_analysis.py`

None. Blocks the attribution and trade-off implementation slices.

Parent AC1 and AC2 — this slice defines, in executable form, the attribution split and the trade-off table those ACs require.

# Identify and eliminate the non-proxy client that polls the router `/slots` model-less

**discovered-from:LP-0MVU8003X0018WT8** (AC4 measurement, 2026-11-19)

## Summary

While measuring the AC4 window, a **non-proxy local client** was found opening short-lived loopback connections to the llama-server router (`127.0.0.1:8080`) whose `GET /slots` requests are answered **HTTP 400**. Because llama.cpp logs neither the query string nor a timestamp on that line, the client's identity cannot be recovered from `llama-server.log`, so it is un-attributed today — and it keeps the router-responder `router:400` count non-zero, masking the signal the AC4/AC1 verification depends on.

## Evidence (2026-11-19)

- `scripts/slots_500_triage.py` responder split over the two window files: `router:400 = 1,008` (`llama-server.log-2026-11-19`, 2026-11-18) + `388` (`llama-server.log`, 2026-11-19; 2 of them this session's own probes) with `router:500 = 0` and `child:200 = 99,865`.
- The proxy cannot be the producer: its only model-less `/slots` URL is completed with `?model=` (`proxy/proxy/observability.py:2196-2202`), and `llama_slots_query_failures_total{reason="http_400"}` has **no series at any point in the window** (Prometheus `count by (reason)` returns only `reason="timeout"`).
- Live capture 2026-11-19T15:27–15:31Z: `ss`/`/proc/net/tcp` sampling recorded multiple short-lived ESTABLISHED connections `127.0.0.1:<ephemeral>` → `127.0.0.1:8080` owned by uid 1000, in bursts of 3–16 requests, while the bare-400 count rose 371 → 388. `ss -p` could not resolve the owning pid at sampling resolution, and `sudo` is unavailable in the agent session, so root-owned/podman-host-network ownership was neither confirmed nor excluded.
- Live reproduction of the two permitted producer classes: bare `GET /slots` → 400; `GET /slots?model=does-not-exist` → 400 (identical log line shape).

## Desired outcome

1. **Identify** the client: candidates are a script/cron/timer, an agent-runbook command (`proxy/docs/runbook-5xx.md:52` documents a bare `curl -s http://localhost:8080/slots`, which *provokes* a 400 by design), `scripts/verify_slots_observability.py`'s deliberate bare probe, or a containerised monitor on host networking. Use a root-capable capture (e.g. `ss -tnp` as root, `bpftrace`/`execsnoop`, or `conntrack -E`) to bind the connection to a pid and command line.
2. **Decide** per call site: keep it if it is an intentional negative probe (then exclude it from the triage count / document it), or route it to `?model=<resolved id>` / stop polling if it is incidental.
3. **Document** the outcome in `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` (router vs child responder split, attribution rule) and update the parent item's AC1 re-check ("no non-proxy client polls the router `/slots` directly" — currently does not hold).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The client is named by pid + command line (or explicitly proven to be root/container-owned) with the capture transcript recorded as a comment.
- [ ] Each call site is either fixed (`?model=` / stop polling) or documented as an intentional negative probe that the triage tooling counts separately.
- [ ] `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` records the finding and how to read it in the responder split.
- [ ] Re-measurement after the fix shows `router:400` attributable to zero unexplained events over a fresh window.

## Key Files

- `scripts/slots_500_triage.py`
- `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md`
- `proxy/docs/runbook-5xx.md`
- `scripts/verify_slots_observability.py`
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py`

# Goal

As the producer, I want one recorded decision on what `slots_stale < 5 %` **means** — the delivered
300 s "unusably old" bound, the plan's 2 s freshness value, or both as separate statements — so the
number cannot be quoted as evidence of freshness when it is not.

# Why (the measured ambiguity)

The post-fix 24 h window (`2026-11-18T10:25Z → 2026-11-19T10:25Z`, record
`docs/dev/slots-stale-postfix-window-2026-11-18-to-19.md`) passes the target on the delivered
definition and fails it by ×6.3 on the plan's candidate:

| Definition | Reading | Target |
|---|---|---|
| age > 300 s ceiling (delivered, `max(120, 10 × 30 s cadence)`) | **4.88 %** | < 5 % → **met** |
| age > 2 s (plan Q3 candidate) | **31.60 %** of datable polls | < 5 % → **missed** |
| age p50 / p90 / p99 / max | 0.73 s / 35.14 s / 187.73 s / 424.20 s | — |

81.3 % of the over-2 s polls carry `capacity_hint=prefill_bound`, i.e. the snapshot ages because the
backend is blocked in prefill; no read-path change removes that. The choice is therefore a contract
choice, not a defect fix, and it is the producer's (parent AC2 second branch).

# Options (the decision, not a preference)

1. **Keep 300 s**, and describe `slots_stale` everywhere as an *unusably-old* bound — never as freshness.
2. **Tighten** to a stated value (2 s candidate) with its own re-baselined target, accepting ~32 % today.
3. **Two-tier**: keep `slots_stale` at 300 s (safety bound) and add a separate freshness SLO on
   `slots_snapshot_age_seconds` (candidate 2 s) with its own threshold and report line.

# Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Decision recorded.** This item carries the producer's choice (one of the three options, or
  an explicit alternative) with its rationale and the date.
- **AC2 — Definition written down.** The chosen definition is applied to every place that quotes the
  target: the parent's AC2 text, `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`, and any tracker/doc
  that states `< 5 %` (grep the literal).
- **AC3 — Change is pinned if the threshold moves.** Any ceiling/threshold change ships with a
  relabelling/consistency test (same discipline as LP-0MWM0CSDL008RB1E AC3), and the report labels
  every pre/post figure by the definition that produced it.
- **AC4 — Baselines carried.** The decision note carries the comparable figures side by side:
  2026-10-29 29.59 % and 2026-11-01/02 40.48 % and 2026-11-16/17 18.03 % (all **pre-definition-change**,
  cache-fallback semantics), plus 2026-11-18/19 4.88 % at 300 s and 31.60 % at 2 s (age semantics).
- **AC5 — Downstream informed.** LP-0MWM0CSDL008RB1E (gate redesign) and LP-0MWRXGPO3004GXD7
  (nightly reporting) are pointed at the decision so neither re-litigates it.

# Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` (`local_slots_max_snapshot_age_seconds`, cadence-derived default)
- `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`
- `docs/dev/slots-stale-postfix-window-2026-11-18-to-19.md` + `.json`
- `scripts/slots_snapshot_age_distribution.py`

## Impact

Every future `slots_stale` claim states what it measured, so a passing target can no longer be
mistaken for a freshness guarantee.
